i really tried to give this game a fair chance. i recognise the challenges that come with building a new engine, and i was willing to accept the delay, but the fact that this is the final product after several years of development is incredibly underwhelming.

the engine and graphics are genuinely solid, and they are the one clear improvement over 24, but almost everything else feels like a major regression for the series. the game is plagued with bugs: players entering the pitch in tracksuits, strange ui glitches, frequent crashes, and general instability. it feels like it needed at least another year of development.

the biggest step backwards from 24 to 26 is the ui. i genuinely tried to adapt, but it is a chore to navigate. no ui should require 20+ hours of “getting used to it” before it becomes tolerable. fm24’s ui was nearly perfect and did not need to be changed at all.

i really hope si take the right lessons from this and make obvious improvements for fm27, because a game with fm24’s ui and systems, fm26’s engine, and more depth would be excellent!

Football Manager has always been my favourite gaming franchise — ever since the Championship Manager 01/02 days. I’ve poured thousands of hours into these games over the years. But the fact that I’ve only managed around 12 hours on this latest version since early access says it all — and honestly, six of those hours were just me walking away, hoping I’d come back with a new perspective.

It’s not about the bugs — those can be patched. The real issue is the base game itself. It’s genuinely unplayable for me. The UI is dreadful: cluttered, unintuitive, and painfully “clicky.” Key features and niche details that gave the series its depth have been stripped away.

What made Football Manager great was that you could play it your way. Now, it feels like you’re being forced into one rigid style — Myles’ vision. And it’s painfully clear that this version was designed with a new market in mind: console players. The loyal fanbase that built this franchise? Forgotten, in favour of chasing new coin. Honestly, if i had bought this through steam and not via a 3rd party, i'd of got a refund.

I have loved the Football Manager series for years and I spent countless hours with the previous games. I could play for entire evenings and lose track of time, especially during the transfer windows and when working with the scouting system. That used to be my favourite part of the game and I really enjoyed going deep into every detail. In Football Manager 2026 it feels like all of that has been taken away from me. The game is messy and confusing, the interface is hard to read and navigate, and there are bugs everywhere. Instead of feeling in control of my club, I constantly feel lost in menus that do not make sense. Right now it is just a very frustrating and sad phase as a long time fan, especially because important issues are not being fixed quickly. Overall it is a huge disappointment and I can only hope the developers react soon and bring the game back to the standard it once had.

I've played every single Championship Manager and Football Manager since 1992 (yes I'm that old!) and this is hands-down the worst iteration of the series. (Game time for FM24 stands just under 1300 hours)

I've gone through all the major changes - from text only to 2d dots to 3d generation, multiple interface changes, and they've all had their positive and negative points but this is a huge backwards step. It has been dumbed down in the wrong areas, like player interactions/touchline shouts make you feel like a passenger and over complicated in others. Navigation is all but impossible, you feel like to are fighting the game - squad stats are buried away, and I'm yet to find how to compare players. It no longer feels like a FM game but rather it's a bad console port aimed at the EA/FIFA generation.

FM has lost it's soul with this game and for the first time since Sports Interactive split from Eidos in 2003 I am seriously considering not buying the next FM game
